name: Chinese folk religion
title: The story of Chinese folk religion

text: More than 3,000 years ago, people in China already honoured their ancestors and tried to learn the future.
The religion has no founder and no church: people belong to it through their village, their family group or a temple.
src: ancestor veneration from prehistory and divination by 1250–1150 BCE
founder: none / The prime criterion for taking part is not to believe a doctrine but to belong: to an association, a village or a kinship group

text: Its followers worship many gods and spirits, from gods of mountains and streams to the Stove God of the home.
They believe some gods were once people, like the warrior Guan Yu.
src: The shen, gods or spirits, are forces of growth: gods of nature, of stars, mountains and streams; household gods such as the Stove God
people who became gods, such as the warrior Guan Yu

text: Worshippers offer incense, oil, candles and money to the gods, and make promises called vows.
Families honour their ancestors before special tablets, and all over China at the Qingming Festival.
src: Worshippers offer incense, oil, candles and money, make vows
ancestors are honoured before their tablets and nationally at the Qingming Festival

text: The religion has no holy book of its own, but it draws on many old books, like the Daodejing.
Its followers believe in qi, the energy that all things are made of, and that good deeds bring good rewards.
src: has no canon of its own but draws on a vast heritage of sacred books / the Daodejing
qi, the breath or energy of which all things are made / bao ying, moral reciprocity, by which every being is rewarded according to its deeds

text: More than 600 years ago, the Hongwu Emperor made the worship of the local gods stronger and better organised.
Chinese people who moved abroad took the religion with them, to Southeast Asia and to America.
src: In the 14th century the Hongwu Emperor of the Ming used the name Shendao for the indigenous cults, which he strengthened and systematised
Emigrants carried the religion abroad / Among the Chinese of Southeast Asia / on the American West Coast

text: More than 100 years ago, China's rulers began to attack the religion, and later the Communist Party destroyed many temples.
Since 1978 it has come back: millions of temples have been rebuilt, and hundreds of millions of people follow it today.
src: after the revolution of 1911 most temples were put to other uses or destroyed / After 1949 the Communist Party destroyed temples in anti-superstition campaigns
After the 1978 constitution the religion revived rapidly, with millions of temples rebuilt or built from scratch / it has revived since 1978 among hundreds of millions
